clusters.state_of_play: A major earthquake (7.4 magnitude, strongest to hit Colombia this century, epicentre in Chocó region) has killed at least 285 people, injured more than 4,000, with approximately 400 missing. Tens of thousands of homes have been damaged, leaving many Colombians sleeping in shelters or outside. The earthquake has affected more than 100,000 people. The critical 72-hour survival window has passed but rescue teams continue digging, with a survivor found nearly four days after the quake. Rescuers are calling for silence around rubble sites to listen for survivors. Firefighters rescued a trapped dog from the rubble. Colombia has declared three days of national mourning. Tons of aid from regional partners have begun arriving. Rescue operations continue in Cali, Pereira, and the Chocó region; a woman was pulled alive from a collapsed hotel in Pereira after 36 hours. The US Fairfax County Urban Search and Rescue Team has deployed a 10-person contingent. Mexican volunteer group Topos Azteca has arrived in Colombia to assist, but Colombia separately rejected Mexico's military rescue team — Mexico said its military rescuers were refused entry, while Colombia denies politics played a role. Hospitals in Cali sustained damage, forcing medical staff to prioritize critical patients. Civilian databases still estimate ~4,000 missing versus the official figure of ~400. Conspiracy theories falsely blaming an Alaska research program for the earthquake have spread on social media. Colombia is now grappling with the rebuilding phase; the Chocó region, predominantly Afro-Colombian and Indigenous, faces deepening hunger and homelessness according to its governor, while Colombian superstar Shakira visited affected areas and pledged to help build at least 10 new schools.
